contract: Per-file counts for the no-padding and requirement-binding invariants. `padded` and `undefined` are ALLOWANCES and may only ever go DOWN; a file absent from `files` is allowed ZERO, and once both totals reach 0 this repo is enforced at absolute zero automatically. Raising either is a gate failure -- see coverage-shrink-waivers.json (requirement_id 'baseline:<path>') if a raise is genuinely intended. `unbound` is VISIBILITY ONLY and is never a pass/fail lever: gating on it would reward a bulk script that attaches plausible requirement ids to untouched rows, turning an honest unbound count into dishonest traceability. Bindings added to a row whose executable substance did not change are rejected by the separate manufactured_binding check, which needs no baseline.
atom_contract: `atoms` maps each requirement id to the canonical body hashes bound to it. A coverage ATOM is the PAIR (requirement_id, hash). Deleting duplicate rows that share an atom removes NO atom and is always permitted -- that is why padding deletion needs no waiver. Losing the LAST atom of an active requirement is blocked unless matrix-integrity-ledger.json carries a rekey, an enumerated equivalent-or-stronger replacement, or a tombstone with a fixed reason code. Every binding here is CANDIDATE, not VERIFIED: none has survived a mutation/negation test, because nothing in this corpus has ever executed.
